description:
Override `MetadataBackend::get_metadata_changes` in `MemoryBackend` so the destroyed array (and the created/updated arrays without a re-fetch) honor `filterRelatedType` and `filterMetadataType` per draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §3.3.

This requires extending `ChangeEntry` in memory.rs:89 to carry the (related_type, type_name) tuple per recorded Id, populated at `create_object`/`update_object`/`destroy_object` time when the metadata is fresh in hand. The override then walks the change log and filters all three arrays in a single pass — no get_objects re-fetch.

Sites:
  - crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/memory.rs:89 — extend `ChangeEntry`
  - Same file at `create_object` (~line 571), `update_object` (~line 638), and `destroy_object` (~line 665) — search `change_log_mut`. For destroy, capture (related_type, type_name) from the object's stored JSON BEFORE removing it from `objects`.
  - New override of `get_metadata_changes` from .5.1's trait method on `impl MetadataBackend for MemoryBackend`.

Sketch:

    #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
    struct ChangeRecord {
        id: Id,
        related_type: String,
        type_name: String,
    }

    #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
    struct ChangeEntry {
        new_state: u64,
        created: Vec<ChangeRecord>,
        updated: Vec<ChangeRecord>,
        destroyed: Vec<ChangeRecord>,
    }

At each `change_log_mut(...).push(...)` site, fill related_type and type_name from the live `Metadata` value. The existing get_changes impl in memory.rs:349 needs to be updated to map ChangeRecord → Id (currently uses Vec<Id> directly).

Override:

    async fn get_metadata_changes(
        &self,
        _caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        since_state: &jmap_types::State,
        max_changes: Option<u64>,
        filter_related_type: Option<&str>,
        filter_metadata_type: Option<&[String]>,
    ) -> Result<ChangesResult, BackendChangesError<Self::Error>> {
        // Walk the change log from since_state, filter each ChangeRecord
        // by (related_type, type_name) against the supplied filter args,
        // collect Ids per array. Reuse the existing has_more_changes /
        // max_changes logic from get_changes::<Metadata>.
    }

## Acceptance
  - Existing test `changes_filter_related_type_drops_non_matching_created` still passes (verifies override is consistent with handler-level behavior for created/updated).
  - New test `changes_filter_drops_non_matching_destroyed` against MemoryBackend: create a Metadata of relatedType=Email, destroy it, create another of relatedType=Mailbox, destroy it, /changes with `filterRelatedType: Email` and assert only the first destroyed Id appears.
  - New test `changes_filter_combined_related_type_and_metadata_type` against MemoryBackend asserts AND semantics on the destroyed array.
  - Handler doc comment at metadata.rs:49-60 (from .5.1) updated to note that the workspace's reference MemoryBackend now achieves strict §3.3 conformance via its override.
  - `cargo test --workspace` clean.
  - `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.

## Out of scope
  - Trait method shape (→ .5.1; this bead consumes that shape).
  - Performance benchmarks for the change log walk (separate; benches epic).

## Depends on
  Blocks on .5.1. Parent: JMAP-06zp.3.5.
title: MemoryBackend strict §3.3 conformance: override get_metadata_changes, extend ChangeEntry
